sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental law; unitary national system based on the Civil Code, Commercial Code, and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States Tax Convention of 20 December 1996
Luxembourg-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1996, in force 1997)
EU TFEU (freedom of establishment and provision of services)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 22 July 2021 restricting access to a legitimate-interest basis; CSSF Regulation 12-02 on AML/CFT for professionals of the financial sector; and applicable Grand-Ducal implementing regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of every UBO, director (gérant), and shareholder of record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy accepted locally; if a foreign civil-status certificate is required, Hague Apostille for 1961 Convention states, otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official register excerpt of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial register or company registry in the shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention state) or consular legalization (non-Convention state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-conviction (extrait de casier judiciaire) for each natural-person manager and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority of the manager's or UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; French, German, or English translation certified by a sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and declaration of lawful source of funds for the contribution to capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The client's bank (original or certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature notarized in the country of origin and apostilled or legalized if the bank is outside the EU/EEA; EU/EEA bank letters may be certified by a Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or domiciliation agent contract) and, where applicable, a letter of consent from the landlord or domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Landlord or licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent (PSF)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Delivered in original; lease agreement notarized or countersigned before a Luxembourg notary if foreign-made

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of shareholders, UBOs, gérants, and acting counsel against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List (for USD-related flows), the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance frozen assets list, and PEP databases (e.g., World-Check or Dow Jones); risk-based enhanced due diligence (EDD) on PEPs and on persons connected to FATF or CRF high-risk jurisdictions; suspicious transaction reports to be filed with the Luxembourg Cellule de Renseignement Financier within 24 hours of suspicion; all records retained for five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) online portal, https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin script (French, German, or Luxembourgish, or a transliterated Latin version for foreign-language names); it must contain the legal-form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' or 'S.à r.l.'; the name must not be confusingly similar to an existing RCSL-registered name and must comply with Luxembourg public-policy and decency requirements.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: OPC; UCITS; Fonds commun de placement
Chambre de Commerce; Chamber of Commerce
European; Euro (if implying a misleading institutional or EU-flag connection); Croix-Rouge; Red Cross
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: the RCSL reservation is not extendable; if incorporation is not completed within 60 days, the name is released and a new reservation application (with re-payment of the fee) may be filed unless a conflicting name was meanwhile registered. Rejection and appeal: the RCSL notification states the specific refusal ground; the applicant may (i) correct the name and file a fresh reservation, or (ii) institute an administrative appeal to the Tribunal administratif within three months of notification under the Law of 1 December 1978 on non-contentious administrative procedure, attaching the negative decision and the corrected name evidence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual address (PO box) is not permissible. A licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent (bank or PSF) may provide a registered office, but the SARL must retain real administrative substance proportionate to its activity (local management, decision-making records, and operational or outsourcing arrangements); remote-screen-support and IoT-telemetry businesses relying solely on a domiciliation address without a local gérant or payroll face OECD/EU substance scrutiny and higher CRF attention.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Baseline estimated at 5%-15% within the first 24 months for a standard low-risk ISIC 6201 SARL; the probability rises to more than 50% if the registered office hosts in excess of 50 unrelated companies, the company has no local payroll or local decision-maker, or the AML/KYC file triggers a CRF or CSSF field visit; low-risk remote software firms can mitigate this through a professional fiduciary, local accounting records, and documented substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL/LBR name reservation (fixation de dénomination) and pre-clearance search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff issued by the RCSL (EUR 25 per reservation).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed for SARL incorporation, including the articles of association and UBO attestation per the Law of 13 January 2019
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary registered in the Barreau de Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff and round-sum charge; market benchmark EUR 2,000-2,500 for a standard SARL with minimum capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL registration and publication in the electronic official gazette (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / Ministry of Justice (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration and publication fees (approx. EUR 250-320 combined).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) initial UBO declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Ministry of Justice / LBR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No filing fee imposed; declaration legally required within one month of incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions database screens (World-Check or Dow Jones) for all natural persons
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML screening provider, notary, and legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription rate passed through; estimated at EUR 15-30 per natural person screened.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate records, passports, criminal records, and bank letters
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille-issuing authority in the foreign state (e.g., Secretary of State or Ministry of Foreign Affairs) or consular services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document statutory fees in the issuing state (EUR 10-60 per apostille or legalization, plus courier and sworn translation).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO-piercing analysis, and purpose-limitation/KYC memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Luxembourg law firm (Barreau de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee under engagement letter; alternative time-charge at prevailing Luxembourg rates (EUR 280-420 per hour).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation service, first year, payable in advance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed PSF fiduciary or domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of EUR 1,200-1,500 per year, plus VAT.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (notably by the Law of 10 August 2016 on company law modernization), Articles 710-1 et seq. (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), operator of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), under the supervision of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) containing the articles of association (statuts), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum (approx. USD 13,000); share capital must be fully subscribed; each share must be paid up to at least 25% of its nominal value at incorporation; funds must be deposited with a Luxembourg or EU credit institution and blocked until RCS registration (attestation de blocage de fonds) or held in notarial escrow; in-kind contributions are permitted subject to valuation and description in the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SHAREHOLDER AND MANAGER OF THE SOCIÉTÉ À RESPONSABILITÉ LIMITÉE: Share subscription: the subscription of the issued share capital of EUR 12,000 is ratified; the statutory minimum payment per share is confirmed and the bank blocking attestation accepted. Registered office: the address in the articles of association is adopted as the registered office for all statutory, tax and administrative purposes. Officers: the first manager (gérant) is appointed and vested with full authority to file the incorporation deed, complete RCS registration and RESA publication, open bank and payment accounts, and file all tax and social security declarations. The manager may perform any ancillary act to bring the company into operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Verification and Pre-Registration Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — online RCS name search portal (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a negative and positive name search in the RCS database to verify that the proposed name (e.g., '[Proposed Name] S.à r.l.') is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Luxembourg company, does not contain prohibited terms, and is compatible with the company object; the name receives definitive protection upon RCS registration; the notary must reconfirm availability in the deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and at least two alternative names
Summary of the company object (ISIC 6201 remote desktop and IoT telemetry software)
Identification details of shareholders (full name, address, date of birth)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for identity or similarity with an earlier registration, instruct the notary to file a fresh request with an amended name or submit written observations to LBR within 15 days for re-examination; amend the draft articles accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Capital Blocking Account and Deposit of Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, Spuerkeess) or the notary's escrow account (compte séquestre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary current account in the name of the 'S.à r.l. in formation'; transfer the fully subscribed minimum capital (EUR 12,000, with at least 25% paid on each share); obtain a blocking attestation from the bank committing it to release funds only against presentation of the final RCS registration extract; if the bank refuses, the notary may hold the funds on escrow.
required_dossiers: KYC identification of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Bank account application forms and source-of-funds evidence
Short activity description or business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC or source-of-funds documentation, supplement the file before re-submission; if the application is ultimately rejected, apply with another Luxembourg credit institution or use the notary's escrow account without restarting the incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) competent for the district of the registered office, under the Ministry of Justice (notariat)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary drafts the deed of incorporation and statutes, verifies the name availability printout and the capital blocking attestation, checks the legality of the object and the capacity of the parties, authenticates the deed upon attendance or power of attorney of the shareholders, and collects the regulated notarial fee; legal personality is acquired only upon RCS registration, not upon signature.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking attestation or notarial escrow receipt
Valid passport or identity document of shareholders and manager (gérant)
Draft statutes approved by the parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution due to missing evidence or non-compliant clauses, remedy the identified defect, adjust the statutes or UBO declarations, and reschedule the signature session; no administrative appeal lies against a notary, but another notary may be instructed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), in coordination with the Administration des contributions directes (ACD); official portal: Guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL, the company obtains its Luxembourg national registration number and business identification through the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) at incorporation. VAT registration is made separately with the AEDT through the MyGuichet/eTVA portal using the standard VAT registration application. A non-established foreign entity supplying taxable services in Luxembourg with no place of business in Luxembourg must register for Luxembourg VAT before commencing such supplies if no reverse charge or OSS mechanism applies; a Luxembourg-established SARL must register when annual taxable turnover excluding VAT exceeds the statutory small-enterprise threshold and may also voluntarily register below that threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the SARL is regarded as a fully taxable corporate entity subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; it is not fiscally transparent).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no United States-style check-the-box election. Entity classification follows the legal form under Luxembourg law. Taxable persons may elect VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under the conditions of the Luxembourg VAT law; corporate income tax consolidation/fiscal unity is available for qualifying 95%-owned Luxembourg resident subsidiaries provided the relevant statutory conditions are met. ATAD hybrid mismatch rules apply automatically and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover excluding VAT for Luxembourg-established small enterprises; non-established foreign suppliers have no turnover threshold and are registrable from the first taxable transaction unless reverse charge or OSS applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time electronic invoicing clearance, digital stamping or continuous transaction control regime is currently in force. Invoices must satisfy EU VAT invoicing requirements; B2G e-invoicing uses the PEPPOL standard where mandated for public procurement suppliers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported to destinations outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT where the supplier retains valid proof that the goods left the EU in accordance with Luxembourg export rules. For remote screen sharing and IoT software services supplied to a non-EU business customer, Luxembourg VAT does not apply under the B2B place-of-supply rule (taxable at the customer's jurisdiction), which operates commercially as zero-rating; B2C digital services are subject to the destination-state OSS mechanism rather than the export zero-rating regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic Single Administrative Document)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR transport document
Commercial invoice and underlying contract/purchase order
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement showing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where export zero-rating is improperly claimed, the AEDT may assess the VAT previously zero-rated, add statutory late interest, and impose administrative penalties for incorrect declarations; intentional fraudulent conduct may additionally expose the taxpayer to criminal prosecution under Luxembourg tax and criminal law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); monetary authority and member of the Eurosystem. Foreign exchange and financial-sector conduct supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the competent AML/CFT supervisor for banks and payment institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full eurozone convertibility with no residual capital or current account exchange controls. The EU Treaty, the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements, and the EU Capital Movements Directive (Directive 88/361/EEC, as implemented) guarantee unrestricted cross-border flows between Member States and third countries, subject only to EU sanctions and BCL statistical reporting obligations. Dividend and profit repatriation are not subject to currency licences or FX authorisation; applicable hurdles are solely tax-related (Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at 15% subject to treaty relief and the Parent-Subsidiary Directive) and standard banking due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender exists in Luxembourg, nor is there any statutory conversion ratio or repatriation deadline. Export receipts may be held in freely convertible EUR or foreign currencies within legally opened bank accounts. Exporters are required to report cross-border transaction data to the BCL for statistical balance-of-payments purposes under the BCL Regulation concerning external statistics; reporting is informational and does not impose exchange control obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Foreign Currency Treasury Account
Commercial Operational Account / FX Hedging Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkees)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. An offshore fintech or electronic money institution (EMI) holding a valid e-money or payment institution licence in the EEA can passport into Luxembourg and open a settlement account at a Luxembourg credit institution or at the BCL (where applicable). Non-EEA EMIs without a passport must rely on a Luxembourg-licensed agent, an EU branch, or a partnership with a local credit institution. Digital EMI-only onboarding is accepted by some Luxembourg banks, but the foreign EMI must demonstrate regulatory substance, compliance with CSSF AML/CFT outsourcing rules, and auditable transaction monitoring. For a low-risk software company collecting via Stripe/Paddle, using an EMI as a collection gateway is viable while the primary treasury account remains at a tier-1 Luxembourg bank to ensure clearing reliability and Local File tax documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks typically require at least one authorised representative (usually the managing director or a designated signatory) to attend an in-person or video-verified due-diligence interview. Physical presence in Luxembourg is the most reliable onboarding route; a remote opening is legally possible under the CSSF-AML/CFT framework if the bank applies video identification with biometric liveness check, digital signature via LuxTrust, and receives counsel-certified corporate documents. For non-EU shareholders or directors, banks often insist on physical attendance at a branch or at a LuxTrust notary office to mitigate identity and reputational risk. The final decision rests with each bank's KYC committee, and a remote-only opening for a foreign-owned Luxembourg SARL without any local presence generally receives a lower viability rating unless an existing relationship with the bank is maintained.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) with non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated LU Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés excerpt with shareholder registry, full UBO declaration to CSSF (RBE), apostilled and translated certificates of incorporation or equivalent for each natural-person beneficial owner, and five years of audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border software revenue with high payment-processor chargeback rates or multiple third-country clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed annual recurring revenue schedule, executed client contracts for remote screen-share and IoT telemetry software, payment processor statements (Stripe/Paddle) showing transaction justification, domestic and EU VAT records, chargeback ratio below 1%, and a written cyber-security policy demonstrating no sanctioned-jurisdiction usage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions routed through high-risk or non-OECD counterparties for trade disbursements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, signed purchase agreements, shipping and service-delivery evidence, beneficial ownership declaration of the receiving entity, sanctions list screening report, and reasoned written commercial justification covering the nature and ultimate end-use of the software or telemetry hardware.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound equity-capital injection from a related group without clear business purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes approving capital increase, share subscription agreement, swift transfer message containing the BCL balance-of-payments purpose code, bank reference letter of the sending group company, intercompany loan or contribution agreement (as applicable), and confirmation that the funds do not originate from crypto exchanges or unregulated lending platforms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the SARL's Luxembourg operational account using a BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for capital participation (commonly code 701 for direct equity investment or intercompany loan code 703). The sending institution is required to write the shareholder reference, the nature of the transfer ('equity contribution', 'shareholder loan', 'cash-pool contribution'), and the UBO of the sending entity in Field 70 of the MT103. Simultaneously, the SARL's Luxembourg counsel or accountant must record the contribution in the commercial register and update the annual financial statement; banks typically verify the registration and may request a share certificate or loan agreement before crediting the full amount. Beneficiary account verification is mandatory: the bank will name-match the receiving entity against sanctions and PEP lists, and the transaction is cleared via TARGET2 for EUR or via SWIFT correspondent banks for USD/GBP and other currencies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for software reseller commissions, hardware procurement, subcontracting, and licencing fees are cleared primarily through the European TARGET2 system in EUR using SEPA Credit Transfer or SWIFT MT103 for foreign currencies. For larger or documentary trade transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) opened by the Luxembourg bank provides secure settlement to the supplier's bank, while MT202/MT202COV relays are used for bank-to-bank customer credit transfers. Daily treasury liquidity is controlled through multi-currency accounts at the tier-1 bank, with predefined approval limits, dual-signature mandates, and automated positive-pay reconciliation. Vendor disbursements to non-EU counterparties require a valid OCRA/FATCA self-certification, VAT invoice, and if applicable a certificate of residence to avoid domestic withholding tax; all transfers must include accurate ISO purpose codes and a contractual reference to satisfy the bank's transaction-monitoring obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX transactions for immediate settlement of foreign currency trade payables and receivables
Outright FX forwards (vanilla forwards) with maturity up to 12 months to hedge EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF exposure
FX swaps (swap-out/swap-in) for short-term liquidity rebalancing between EUR and major currencies
Cross-currency swaps (interest-rate and principal exchange) for longer-dated treasury efficient hedging, subject to EMIR reporting and initial-margin thresholds

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) involving non-convertible or lightly regulated emerging-market currencies, executed only with a licensed counterparty and documented as a true hedge of actual software export or input-procurement exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements deposit with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/eJustice, Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of shareholder approval of accounts and no later than 8 months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice from the RCS registrar; administrative fine up to €5,000; request from Public Prosecutor to compel filing; possible court-ordered compliance and, after repeated default, risk of administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the year following the relevant tax year (extendable to 31 December for electronic filings through MyGuichet)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment on estimated taxable basis; late filing penalty of 10% on assessed tax; monthly late-payment interest at 0.5% per month; additional administrative fines and tax criminal sanctions for gross negligence or fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / local commune tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as corporate income tax return – 31 May following tax year, extendable to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty and late-payment interest of 0.5% per month; municipal tax surcharge assessments; compulsory collection by the tax authority

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same annual deadline as corporate income tax return – 31 May following tax year, extendable to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic assessment on taxable net wealth; 10% late-filing penalty; monthly late-payment interest; enforcement proceedings and tax liens on business assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit required if the SARL exceeds two of the following three criteria as at the balance sheet date for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average headcount > 50 full-time equivalent. Audit also required for public-interest entities, undertakings raising public debt, or where shareholders representing at least 10% of subscribed capital exercise the legal request option.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial and annual accounts and implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for non-listed companies and mandatory for certain financial institutions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg has no separate annual UBO filing deadline; the beneficial owner declaration must be filed with the Register des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) within 1 month of any change. The RBE information must remain accurate and current at all times, and the SARL must, on an ongoing basis, maintain a paper register of beneficial owners. The annual shareholders' meeting approval of accounts serves as a trigger for reviewing shareholding transfers and updating the RBE and share transfer register. Failure to keep RBE data current exposes the SARL and directors to criminal fines and imprisonment under the Luxembourg AML/CTF Law of 13 January 2019.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' meetings and board decisions
Register of beneficial owners (as maintained under the 2019 UBO Law)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 – 1,650 (EUR 200 – 1,500) per annum for standard registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,600 – 16,500 (EUR 6,000 – 15,000) for a typical mandatory statutory audit of a mid-size Luxembourg SARL; small companies below audit thresholds may incur only review or compilation fees of USD 2,200 – 5,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg applies the standard corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) of 17% plus a 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT base, and a 6.75% municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) in Luxembourg City, yielding an aggregate statutory headline rate of 24.94%. Preferential regimes include the intellectual property (IP) box regime, providing an 80% exemption on qualifying net income derived from qualifying IP assets, resulting in an effective rate of approximately 5.09% for qualifying IP income. Additional incentives include the R&D tax credit, investment tax credits for tangible and intangible assets, and the participation exemption regime for qualifying shareholdings, which fully exempts qualifying dividend income and capital gains from corporate income tax. The minimum net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) is EUR 4,815 per annum for entities exposed to the minimum tax regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaires 2000 / 2001 / 2002 and electronic filing via the Luxembourg tax authority's eCDF portal (Guichet.lu eSpace / MyGuichet)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end, unless an extension is granted by the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes). For a SARL with a calendar fiscal year, the deadline is 31 December of the subsequent year. The tax assessment (bulletin de l'impôt) is issued after review, and provisional payments are generally due quarterly on the 10th of February, May, August, and November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, legal form (SARL), registered office address, and national business register number (RCS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARLs with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must provide the local PE address and the tax identification number assigned by the Luxembourg tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable profit comprising Luxembourg-source and worldwide business income attributable to the Luxembourg entity or PE, after commercial-law adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income; include only PE-attributable profits and specific Luxembourg-source items such as certain royalties and real estate rental income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax base calculated on the unified taxable net wealth, subject to exemptions and allowances (e.g., the EUR 500,000 allowance for qualifying shareholdings).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE assets situated in Luxembourg are included in the Luxembourg net wealth tax base; foreign assets are excluded unless effectively connected to the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of qualifying shareholdings for which the participation exemption is claimed on dividends and capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not required to complete Box 3a; the participation exemption applies at the Luxembourg entity or PE level, not to the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the 80% IP box deduction on qualifying IP income, subject to nexus ratio calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities may claim the IP box only for IP assets effectively connected to a Luxembourg PE and where the underlying R&D, development or enhancement activities or the ownership and management of the IP are performed by the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of intra-group transactions, transfer pricing adjustments, and any adjustments related to thin-capitalisation or interest limitation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with a Luxembourg PE must file transfer pricing documentation for all PE-attributable intercompany dealings with the foreign head office or affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of withholding taxes borne on Luxembourg-source dividends, interest, and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must attach TRC and any DTA relief certificates when claiming reduced withholding tax rate treaty benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Election to offset current-year profits against prior-year tax losses carried forward, subject to the 5-year limitation and change-of-control restriction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses sustained by a Luxembourg PE of a non-resident entity may be carried forward within the 5-year window, limited to profits deriving from the same PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of distributions, redemption payments, and other profit repatriations to shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident majority shareholders must identify their country of tax residence and the applicable DTA provision to support reduced dividend WHT relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from EUR 100 to EUR 50,000, with a progressive daily surcharge of 0.6% of the tax due for each commenced month of delay, capped at 10% of the total tax due. Intentional non-filing can trigger a penalty of EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000 and criminal prosecution for tax evasion, including imprisonment of up to 5 years for the responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the Luxembourg-resident entity or the non-resident beneficiary must submit a completed withholding tax relief application to the Luxembourg tax authority (Administration des contributions directes) at least 10 days prior to the effective distribution date. The application must include a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the residence state tax authority, confirming treaty residence and beneficial ownership. Where no prior clearance is obtained, the withholding agent must apply the statutory 15% rate, and the beneficiary may subsequently file for a refund through the Luxembourg tax authority's refund procedure, attaching the TRC and a treaty eligibility statement. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief may be applied at source if the parent entity is a qualifying EU tax-resident company and satisfies the 10% (or lower reduced threshold applying under grandfathering) shareholding requirement, plus a 12-month minimum holding period condition.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties is 0% for qualifying patent, know-how, and copyright royalties under Luxembourg domestic law. However, under the Luxembourg EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (ATAD) implementation, royalty payments to related non-resident entities that are subject to a preferential regime or not adequately taxable in the recipient state may be recharacterised as deemed Luxembourg-source income and subjected to a 15% withholding tax unless treaty relief applies. Interest withholding tax is generally 0% under Luxembourg domestic law, but payments to related entities in non-cooperative or low-tax jurisdictions may be recharacterised and taxed at 15% unless a tax treaty provides a lower rate. The main DTA rates are 5% or 0% for dividends (with 10% or 25% shareholding thresholds applicable under specific treaties), 0% for most interest, and 0% or 5% for royalties depending on the treaty and IP type.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 500,000 for intercompany cross-border transactions involving tangible goods, services, royalties, or financial transactions in the aggregate; EUR 1,000,000 for intercompany services or financing transactions where the total compensation exceeds the threshold; however, entities with transactions exceeding EUR 4,500,000 in gross revenue or with related-party transactions exceeding EUR 1,500,000 must keep full Local File documentation. The Luxembourg Master File is required where the multinational group has consolidated revenue exceeding EUR 50,000,000 and has at least one Luxembourg entity exceeding the EUR 1,500,000 related-party transaction threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are fully applicable under Luxembourg's domestic tax framework and are reinforced by the OECD BEPS Actions 8-10, the EU ATAD implementation, and the EU Code of Conduct Group. For a Luxembourg SARL conducting remote desktop access and telemetry software activities, substance documentation must demonstrate that the entity maintains real decision-making power, employs adequate qualified staff (IT engineers, product managers, and technical support personnel) located in Luxembourg, incurs substantive R&D and operational expenditures at a level consistent with the functions and risks assumed, and controls and manages the core income-generating activities from Luxembourg. Mere technical ownership of IP or receiving intercompany service fees without substantial managerial, operational, and financial substance will be challenged under the Luxembourg general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) and the ATAD preferred-regime provisions, potentially resulting in reclassification of income, denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT), imposition of penalties, and the activation of Luxembourg's controlled foreign corporation (CFC) rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting or understating taxable revenue from remote screen-share software subscription fees, deliberately manipulating the transfer pricing of intercompany royalty or service payments, or using artificial arrangements to shift profits to no-tax or low-tax jurisdictions without commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion penalties range from EUR 5,000 to EUR 100,000 per offence and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years, plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month and a penalty of 10% of the evaded tax. In aggravated cases involving cross-border manoeuvres or false documentation, the fine may reach EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the manager (gérant) of the SARL may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they fail to file required returns, knowingly authorise false filings, or misappropriate corporate funds. Under Luxembourg company law and tax law, the corporate veil may be pierced where the SARL is used as a facade or where the manager acted manifestly beyond the corporate interest, leading to joint and several liability for the full tax debt, civil restitution to the tax authority, potential travel bans (interdiction de voyage), a 10-year prohibition on managing a Luxembourg corporate entity, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company with no real physical office in Luxembourg, no payroll for local staff, no board meetings in Luxembourg, and performing only passive holding or invoicing functions while the actual remote-support software development, technical support, and sales activity are fully managed from a foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may recharacterise and reallocate the entire taxable profit to the foreign beneficial owner, disallow the deduction of intercompany payments, apply a 15% non-resident dividend WHT on deemed distributions, and impose a daily surcharge of EUR 1,000 for failure to maintain adequate substance records under the Luxembourg substance-related information exchange framework. Additionally, the entity may be stripped of its tax residence certificate and lose treaty benefits under the OECD Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The manager and any de facto director can be personally assessed for 100% of the re-determined Luxembourg tax liability, be subject to a civil penalty of EUR 10,000 to EUR 50,000, face travel restrictions to prevent asset dissipation, and may be personally prosecuted for abuse of law (abus de droit) with imprisonment up to 3 years. The Luxembourg tax authority may also obtain a provisional attachment order against the personal bank accounts of directors in cases of fraudulent substance deficiency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Advising clients on the use of shell entities to hide beneficial ownership, deliberately allowing unverified third parties to use the remote screen-share technology to move funds for opaque or sanctioned entities, or failing to file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) where the software platform is used in connection with suspected tax fraud, money laundering, or sanctions evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML law (Loi du 12 novembre 2004, as amended), fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 5,000,000 can be imposed on the legal entity and its responsible officers, in addition to administrative sanctions up to EUR 1,000,000 and licence revocation where applicable. The FIU may freeze the entity's bank accounts and the competent supervisory authority (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) can issue a public warning and a prohibition to exercise certain commercial activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the entity's AML fines, damage claims by third parties, and in cases of gross negligence or intentional conduct, may face imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years. Personal travel bans may be imposed during the investigation and the directors may be disqualified from serving as an administrator or manager of any Luxembourg regulated entity for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring intra-group fees for software licences, technical support, management services, or interest on intercompany loans at prices that materially deviate from the arm's-length standard without contemporaneous documentation; or placing high-profit IP in a Luxembourg shell with no real R&D activity while the actual development occurs in a non-EU low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration is empowered under Article 56bis LIR to perform primary and secondary transfer pricing adjustments, add back excessive deductions, and apply a 5% late-payment interest charge on the additional assessment. A negligence penalty of EUR 250 to EUR 25,000 may be imposed where the documentation is absent or defective; in cases of gross negligence, the penalty rises to 50% of the additional assessed tax plus late-payment interest. The entity also faces potential double taxation absent mutual agreement procedure (MAP) relief and mandatory disclosure of reportable cross-border arrangements under DAC6.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign tax returns containing manipulated transfer pricing are personally liable for the resulting additional tax, penalties, and interest, and can be criminally prosecuted for tax evasion if the manipulation is knowing and intentional. The court may impose civil sanctions including a temporary ban on serving as a director of a Luxembourg company and a reimbursement order for the benefit improperly obtained from the mispriced transactions.
